items.title: Carmen Caramanica interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, July 27, 2011
items.q: Herb Ellis said the same thing.

ctx.x: really don’t know which way is up, which way is down. So we say “try singing the note when you’re playing it.” Okay. So they’ll play and sing the first note and then “what’s the next note?” and you make them sing it, and now where is that, it’s over here. And so by doing this they start to sing what they play. And this goes back to another war story, which is when I first discovered that was a good way to develop the brain-instrument relationship so you’re really playing what you’re hearing not just what you…

Well I’ve heard other people — Herb Ellis said the same thing. He said you should be singing — be able to sing what you want to play I guess. But he apparently did the same thing, he would sing along. So did you eventually get burned out with the road and being away?

You know I did and I think a lot of it had to do with I kind of made a choice to become a career musician rather than a dedicated artist. And this is something that happens to a lot of people. If you’re lucky enough to play the kind of music professionally that you want to play to the exclusion of everything else, then you’re dedicated to your craft, you’re dedicated to your art, and you go where that takes you. But you’re happy doing what you’re doing and you’re not worried about well let’s see I have to support…
